reservations.title: Effect of a saffron extract on sleep quality in adults with moderate insomnia: A decentralized, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
reservations.source_title: Effect of a saffron extract on sleep quality in adults with moderate insomnia: A decentralized, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
reservations.abstract: A three-arm decentralized randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial enrolled 165 adults reporting moderate insomnia to compare a standardized saffron extract at 20 mg or 30 mg daily against placebo over four weeks. The primary outcome was change in Athens Insomnia Scale symptoms; secondary outcomes included self-rated sleep quality, perceived stress, mood, sleepiness and quality of life. Among 150 completers, the saffron groups combined had a modestly greater adjusted improvement in insomnia symptoms than placebo (difference -0.95, 95% CI -1.79 to -0.11). Both doses showed improvements in some self-rated sleep quality and stress comparisons. Several other secondary measures did not significantly differ. No serious adverse events were reported. Interpretation is limited by short follow-up, self-report outcomes and sponsor involvement.
reservations.relevance_reason: Human randomized trial of a specified saffron preparation for insomnia and perceived stress, with mixed secondary results and funding caveats relevant to THS sleep evidence.
reservations.study_design: Three-arm randomized double-blind placebo-controlled decentralized trial

study_details.registration: Not independently checked in this intake

outcomes.result: Combined saffron arms showed modest adjusted improvement relative to placebo: difference -0.95; 95% CI -1.79 to -0.11; P<0.05

outcomes.endpoint: Self-reported sleep quality and perceived stress
outcomes.result: Selected secondary between-group comparisons favored each saffron dose after three to four weeks; formulation-specific, self-report endpoints

outcomes.endpoint: Other psychological, sleepiness and quality-of-life secondary measures
outcomes.result: Not all prespecified secondary measures differed significantly between groups

uncertainty.notes: Modest primary difference; short duration; no objective sleep physiology established; subgroup and long-term generalizability unclear.

adverse_effects.reported: No serious adverse events in the four-week trial
adverse_effects.limits: Small, short trial cannot establish rare or long-term safety.

interactions.reported: No direct drug interaction experiment in this study
interactions.limits: No evidence here that saffron is safe with sedatives, antidepressants or other medications.

limitations: Multiple secondary outcomes and incomplete significance across measures

provenance.source: NCBI PubMed indexed original journal article

reservations.title: Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids in Tea and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Tea Intake
reservations.source_title: Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids in Tea and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Tea Intake
reservations.abstract: Investigators used HPLC-MS/MS to measure pyrrolizidine alkaloids and their N-oxides in 63 tea samples from several processing categories. They detected at least one monitored compound in 77.78 percent of samples, with a mean reported level of 17.67 micrograms per kilogram. A margin-of-exposure and Monte Carlo analysis modeled possible dietary risk under assumptions about consumption. These are product-level analytical and simulated exposure findings, not observed liver injury or direct evidence about individual consumers.
reservations.relevance_reason: Direct primary analytical evidence of botanical product contaminants with clear limits on risk interpretation.
reservations.study_design: Cross-sectional product sampling and modeled dietary exposure

study_details.method: HPLC-MS/MS and Monte Carlo exposure modeling

reservations.population: 63 commercial tea samples; simulated consumer exposures
reservations.intervention: Analytical screening of tea for pyrrolizidine alkaloids and N-oxides
reservations.comparator: Tea-processing categories and simulated consumption scenarios
outcomes: 77.78 percent of samples had a detected analyte
Mean detected concentration reported as 17.67 micrograms per kilogram
reservations.uncertainty: Sampling and modeled intake assumptions limit extrapolation to real-world individual health outcomes.
reservations.adverse_effects: Potential toxicological exposure hazard, without clinical adverse events observed in this study.
reservations.limitations: Small product sample; modeled exposure instead of prospective human health outcomes.
